expectations.text: Identifies possible specific knowledge for a flipper
expectations.evidence: Section 1 quotes the definition "knowledge you cannot be trained for" (matches SKILL.md) and lists flipper-specific candidates: 'The eye' (solid wood vs particleboard, maker's marks), 'Local price intuition', 'Transformation skill', 'Market psychology', 'Taste', plus the play-vs-work diagnostic.

expectations.text: Names leverage types and highlights code/media as permissionless
expectations.evidence: 'Naval names four kinds: labor, capital, code and media, and he calls code and media "permissionless leverage."' Each gets a subsection; code and media are labeled '(permissionless, zero marginal cost)'. Matches SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Moves toward equity/ownership rather than trading hours
expectations.evidence: Opens with "You're not going to get rich renting out your time"; 'Step 4: Own equity, meaning a business that runs partly without you' (curated shop, consignment, wholesale, restoration studio) and 'Equity partnerships'.

expectations.text: Uses accountability or long-term games
expectations.evidence: 'Step 2: Move from transactions to long-term games with long-term people' quotes "Play iterated games... compound interest" (exact SKILL.md wording); 'Step 3: Take on accountability by building a name' (risk under your own name).

expectations.text: Gives concrete next steps
expectations.evidence: Five ordered steps: compute real profit/hour and set an aspirational rate (e.g. $75/hr) and delegate below it, build supply/demand relationships (estate agents, designers), named brand, equity business forms, media/courses/tools.

expectations.text: Quotes or paraphrases the desire contract idea
expectations.evidence: Quotes exactly: "Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want." (matches SKILL.md).

expectations.text: States the seek-wealth idea
expectations.evidence: "Seek wealth, not money or status." with definitions: wealth = assets that earn while you sleep, money = how we transfer time and wealth, status = place in the social hierarchy (all match SKILL.md).

expectations.text: Explains one-desire-at-a-time or choosing desires carefully
expectations.evidence: Thread 1: 'His advice is to choose your desires carefully and keep them few, ideally one at a time'; frames wealth as 'one deliberately chosen desire'. Matches SKILL.md 'Pick desires carefully, one at a time'.

expectations.text: Explains wealth as freedom/means to stop playing games
expectations.evidence: Thread 3: wealth is worth seeking because it 'solves money problems and buys back your time and freedom: freedom from having to rent out your hours'; Thread 2 contrasts positive-sum wealth with zero-sum status games; Thread 5 uses the retirement quote (matches SKILL.md).

expectations.text: Mentions peace/happiness being separate from success
expectations.evidence: 'The book insists that success does not earn happiness'; happiness as 'the state when nothing is missing, with peace as happiness at rest'; table separating Wealth (Part I) from Happiness (Part II). All match SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Identifies possible specific knowledge for a flipper
expectations.evidence: Section 1 lists 'Pricing intuition and spotting value' (Broyhill Brasilia, Herman Miller, walnut under paint), 'Taste in transformation', 'Local market microstructure', 'Negotiation and trust'; defines specific knowledge as play-to-you/work-to-others found via curiosity, consistent with SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Names leverage types and highlights code/media as permissionless
expectations.evidence: 'Naval names three kinds of leverage: Labour, Capital, Products with no marginal cost of replication: code and media... it is permissionless.' This matches the book's 'capital, people, and products with no marginal cost of replication (code and media)' and SKILL.md's 'code and media are permissionless leverage'.

expectations.text: Moves toward equity/ownership rather than trading hours
expectations.evidence: Section 3: 'you won't get rich renting out your time... you want to own equity'; stage table ending in '4. Owned assets / products | Equity | Decoupled from your hours'; step 6 'Own equity' (branded resale business, revenue-share partnerships).

expectations.text: Uses accountability or long-term games
expectations.evidence: Step 7 'Take accountability. Naval says to take on risk under your own name'; Section 4 'Play long-term games with long-term people. Repeat dealings compound' (estate sale company, designers). Both consistent with SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Gives concrete next steps
expectations.evidence: Seven numbered concrete steps: track hours per flip vs profit, set an aspirational rate (~$100/hr) and outsource below it, systematise with templates, film every flip, build an email list/site, productise knowledge, own equity.

expectations.text: Quotes or paraphrases the desire contract idea
expectations.evidence: Quotes "Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want" in 2(b), and the 'that you make' variant in the intro. Consistent with SKILL.md.

expectations.text: States the seek-wealth idea
expectations.evidence: 'Wealth side: "Seek wealth, not money or status."' plus wealth defined as assets that earn while you sleep. Matches SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Explains one-desire-at-a-time or choosing desires carefully
expectations.evidence: 2(b): 'The Almanack doesn't prescribe zero desire. It prescribes few, chosen desires. Naval's advice is to pick one big desire at a time and let go of the rest.' Matches SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Explains wealth as freedom/means to stop playing games
expectations.evidence: 2(a): wealth is 'a tool to buy freedom', solves money problems, ends dependence on a boss and selling hours; retirement redefined as stopping 'sacrificing today for an imagined tomorrow'; 2(c) says the wealth advice 'explicitly tells you to avoid status games'. Note: the quote "Wealth is the thing you want... it buys you freedom" is a loose splice that isn't verifiable in SKILL.md, but the idea itself is correct.

expectations.text: Mentions peace/happiness being separate from success
expectations.evidence: 2(e): happiness is 'a skill and a choice' on an 'independent track'; 'getting rich won't fix an unhappy mind'; 'Wealth solves money problems. It doesn't solve happiness problems.' Consistent with SKILL.md 'Success does not earn happiness'.
